HD.rationale: Home Depot is a fundamentally sound business with dominant market position (~17% U.S. home improvement share), strong cash generation ($6.03B operating cash flow in Q1 FY2026, up 39.5% YoY), and a growing Pro ecosystem via SRS/GMS/Mingledorff's acquisitions expanding TAM to $1.2T. However, the near-term trajectory is mixed: Q1 FY2026 showed revenue growth of +4.8% YoY to $41.77B but EPS declined 4.3% YoY to $3.30, with gross margin compressing 75bps to 33.0% due to acquisition mix effects. Operating margin fell to ~11.9% and ROIC declined from 31.3% to 25.4% as integration costs weigh. The company reaffirmed modest FY2026 guidance of ~1% comparable sales growth and flat-to-+4% EPS growth, reflecting a cautious housing environment with 30-year mortgage rates at 6.47% and a lock-in effect suppressing home turnover. Valuation is moderate: P/E of 24.5x sits within its 1-year range (20.3-28.8) and near the lower end, while P/B has compressed significantly from 45-51x to 24.8x as equity grew. The stock trades at 21.1x forward P/E vs. 5-year median of 22.27x, suggesting slight undervaluation. Near-term catalysts are limited: the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act passage is a modest positive, and the Q2 earnings report (Aug 18) could provide clarity on margin trajectory, but Wolfe Research downgraded to Peer Perform on June 23 citing Pro-strategy execution risks. sources_cited.excerpt: Home Depot and Lowe's shares dropped 2.5-3% after the Federal Reserve held interest rates steady; higher mortgage rates (30-year fixed at 6.47%) reduce housing turnover
Lowe's is recommended as the better buy due to its lower valuation metrics, higher projected growth rates (8% sales growth vs. 4% for Home Depot)
Wolfe Research downgraded the stock to Peer Perform, citing housing lock-in uncertainties and the execution risks of the professional-contractor transition
GAAP operating margins to 11.9% and eroded trailing twelve-month Return on Invested Capital (ROIC) to 25.4% from 31.3%
Home Depot's forward 12-month P/E ratio of 21.1X, below its five-year median of 22.27X
21st Century ROAD to Housing Act passed by both chambers of Congress
Home Depot holds approximately 17% of the U.S. home improvement market
$700B+ addressable Pro market; SRS, GMS, Mingledorff's add scale; cross-sell synergies targeted at $400M run-rate in 2026
management anticipates resuming share repurchases once the company achieves an excess cash position, projected for the first half of 2027
